description: Server -> agent frames the Go agent must REFUSE. These are the boundary where a compromised or buggy server meets a host: the session name becomes a `tmux new -A -s` argument, and the config bounds are what stop a server abusing a machine it does not own. A refused frame is logged and dropped; the connection stays up, because the one thing you must always be able to do to a broken agent is talk to it.

cases.why: A space splits one shell argument into two - the narrow character class is the control that keeps a session name from ever becoming a second argument.
`;` ends a command and starts another; if this name ever reached a shell string it would run rm -rf as whoever owns the agent.
`$(...)` executes before the outer command even runs, so substitution has to be refused at the contract rather than escaped downstream.
A session name is also used to build state paths; `../` would walk out of the directory the agent owns.
33 characters, every one of them legal - this case isolates the 32-character bound from the character class, so a port cannot pass by checking only the alphabet.
target has no default of its own - only its fields do. An open frame with no target at all is a malformed request, not a request for defaults.
hostId is the identity everything the agent stores is keyed by; accepting a free-form string would let a typo silently create a second host.
The pin is lower-case hex. Go's %X (or strings.ToUpper) produces a hash that fails this pattern, and the update stops here rather than after the download - which is the cheap place to fail.
63 characters. A hash that is merely close is not a pin, and a prefix match would accept any digest sharing the first 63 nibbles.
heartbeatSec is bounded 1..3600. Zero is a busy loop that pins a core on someone else's machine, and the bound is what limits what a compromised server can push.
gitLimit is bounded 10..2000. 99999 asks the host to walk its whole history every pass - refused for the same reason as above, and refused as a WHOLE frame so no half-applied config survives.

An unknown frame TYPE is rejected even though an unknown FIELD is stripped: the reader cannot guess what an unrecognised command means, so it logs it, drops it, and keeps the connection - never closes it, and never guesses.
